description: A company commander must sign the next seven-day duty board, assigning qualified personnel to four routine control posts and recording the handover controls for each post.

shared_context.S1: The company must publish a seven-day duty board covering an access-control supervisor, a vehicle-dispatch desk, a communications key-control desk, and a clinic liaison post.
shared_context.S2: Capt. Morgan signs the duty board, and each post must have one named primary for the full period from 17 June through 23 June.
shared_context.S3: The company has a standing policy that duty-board entries must identify a qualified primary and include a documented handover at the start of the assignment.
shared_context.S4: At the routine weekly duty-board review, Capt. Morgan asks the personnel, motor pool, signal, and medical representatives to confirm any qualification or availability information before signing.

PF1.text: The current access-control roster shows Sgt. Hall as the only person whose access-control-supervisor certification remains valid through 23 June; 1st Lt. Patel received the updated certification roster this morning, but it has not yet been added to the duty-board working copy.

PF2.text: Cpl. Vega is the only available person in the company with the current vehicle-dispatch qualification for 17-23 June; SFC Romero confirmed the qualification against the motor-pool register today, but the register update is still awaiting the weekly personnel upload.

PF3.text: Spc. Noor is the only current encryption-key custodian available for the entire 17-23 June period; Lt. Okafor verified the custodian appointment with the communications security clerk this morning, but the appointment has not been posted to the company duty board.

PF4.text: Sgt. Ellis completed the required medical-privacy liaison training and is the only available person cleared to serve as the clinic liaison throughout 17-23 June; Lt. Bennett received the clinic training sign-off after the last staff meeting, so it is not on the circulated qualification list.

acceptance_conditions: Sgt. Hall must be assigned as the access-control supervisor.
Cpl. Vega must be assigned to the vehicle-dispatch desk.
Spc. Noor must be assigned to the communications key-control desk.
Sgt. Ellis must be assigned as the clinic liaison.
The duty period must be recorded as 17 June through 23 June.
A handover commitment must exist for each of the four posts.
The qualification information must be cited in the commander's justification.

content_checks.C6: any(c['type'] == 'duty_handover' and c['target'] == 'access_control' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C7: any(c['type'] == 'duty_handover' and c['target'] == 'vehicle_dispatch' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any(c['type'] == 'duty_handover' and c['target'] == 'key_control' for c in commitments)
content_checks.C9: any(c['type'] == 'duty_handover' and c['target'] == 'clinic_liaison' for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The updated certification roster changes the access-control assignment from an open personnel choice to Sgt. Hall, the only person certified through 23 June.
The motor-pool qualification register changes the vehicle-dispatch assignment to Cpl. Vega, the only person qualified and available for the full duty period.
The verified custodian appointment changes the key-control assignment to Spc. Noor, the only available current encryption-key custodian.
The clinic training sign-off changes the clinic-liaison assignment to Sgt. Ellis, the only person cleared for that post throughout 17-23 June.
